what_it_does: KLIMA solves Boolean Satisfiability (SAT) problems — mathematical puzzles that ask whether a set of logical constraints can ever be satisfied simultaneously. Normally, computers solve these by trying combinations in CPU or GPU, but that means fetching the constraints and data from memory over and over, creating a memory bandwidth bottleneck. KLIMA instead uses mixed-signal technology (a hybrid of analog circuits and digital logic) to evaluate logical constraints directly inside the memory chip itself, in single-digit nanoseconds. By computing where the data lives rather than moving data to the processor, it eliminates the traditional "von Neumann bottleneck" — the slowdown caused by shuttling data between the CPU and main memory.
